title: Ask impulse scaffold and probe notes
content:
TL;DR: field patchwork of short, high-frequency customer requests we label ‘impulses’ — tiny friction triggers (latency blips, cost spikes, hallucination patterns) that repeatedly surface as micro-asks. This note stitches ~18 signals from last 6 weeks into a lightweight scaffold for probes (quick experiments) and 3 candidate feature lanes: a latency-defensive fallback, a cheap-embedding fallback, and a prompt-templating heuristics kit.

Context / why this doc: many CS threads are small, actionable, and time-sensitive; they don’t map cleanly to existing roadmap buckets. We want a repeatable way to capture an impulse -> hypothesis -> probe -> success metric flow so eng/product can ship small low-risk mitigations faster.

How we gathered signals (brief):
- Recorded 18 field threads (support tickets + Slack threads + account calls) between 2025-09-20 and 2025-11-06.
- Focused on customers using hosted API and Dedicated pools; 60/40 split hosted/dedicated.
- Tracked asks that mention latency, cost-per-token, inconsistent outputs, and rollout/traffic split problems.
- Quick interviews for 6 accounts (3 mid-market, 3 startups) to validate impact.

Representative customer impulses (quotes preserved with paraphrase):
- "One small latency spike knocks our UX out — users lose context and bounce" — mid-market SaaS, onboarding flow, hosted.
- "We see high token burn on repeated system messages — wish we could cache more aggressively" — AI startup, dedicated pool.
- "When the primary model is slow we need deterministic fallback without losing format" — fintech platform, high security, private deployment.
- "Embeddings cost surprise when we re-embed short changed lines every call" — e-comm search team.

Pattern clustering (emergent themes):
1) Latency fault tolerance (7 signals): customers want graceful and predictable UX during momentary latency increases. Common requests: automatic short-response fallback, progressive rendering, or an explicit 'degraded mode' model with strict token caps.
2) Cost leakage on repeated meta-text (5 signals): repeated system/user prefixes increase cost; ask for smarter prefix caching or server-side canonicalization.
3) Model variant routing & quality drift (4 signals): want easy policy to route to cheaper model when quality acceptable, or quick swap when regressions detected.
4) Embeddings churn (2 signals): need ephemeral-cache vs re-embed logic, and per-route embedding TTLs.

Impact hypothesis (quantitative kinks):
- Latency fallback (small model or canned response) could reduce user bounce by 10-18% for affected flows; estimated cost of feature ~2 person-weeks to implement routing + telemetry.
- Prefix caching (server-side canonicalization) may cut token consumption on some flows by 20-35%; estimated infra work 3–5 weeks including Q/A.
- Per-route embed TTLs reduces embedding API calls up to 40% for search-heavy customers with repeated small queries; low-risk config change (~1 week) and dashboarding.

Proposed quick probes (MVPs):
A) Degraded UX probe (2-week):
- What: Add a route-level setting "degraded_mode=true" that triggers: (a) switch to a low-latency small model for generation, OR (b) return a short canned response + hint to retry.
- Why: validate if deterministic degraded responses keep users engaged compared to full-latency waits.
- Success metric: session continuation rate within 30s improves by +8% on test cohort.
- Risks: poor UX if canned responses are too terse; must flag in telemetry.

B) Server-side prefix canonicalization (3-week):
- What: detect identical system/user prefixes across requests and substitute a tokenized reference + server cache to avoid re-sending full prefix to the model.
- Why: cut token cost for customers with long system prompts (onboarding, legal instructions).
- Success metric: per-customer token volume drop and billing delta tracked over 7 days.
- Dependencies: routing and runtime needs a cache key — discuss with serving-runtime (ENG-serve).

C) Embedding TTL + delta-sync probe (1-week config):
- What: new API param/console toggle for per-route embedding TTL (e.g., 24h, 7d) + a small delta-update flow to re-embed only changed chunks.
- Why: cheap wins for search customers.
- Success metric: embedding calls per session drop >=25% for participating customers.

D) Model-variant fallback policy (4-week spike):
- What: policy that routes to cheap-variant when average lag >X ms for N consecutive requests; includes auto-retry to primary when lag normalizes.
- Why: balance latency and cost without manual intervention.
- Success metric: decrease in 95th percentile latency and fewer manual incident escalations.
- Notes: needs coordination with the routing and optimize teams — also expose to Dedicated customers for explicit pinning.

Operational notes & telemetry suggestions:
- Add a lightweight label on requests flagged as 'impulse-fallback' to track incidence and downstream success.
- Flag tokens saved from prefix caching as a separate billing bucket for transparent customer reporting.
- Dashboard: per-customer baseline token rate + delta post-probe with simple UIs for CS escalation.

Low-effort quick wins we can ship in 1–2 sprints:
- Expose per-route 'embed_ttl' in console and API (backend config + UI toggle).
- Add canned "degraded-mode" templates in the console so CS can configure non-engineered fallbacks for customers.
- Short doc/update: "how to reduce token burn" — checklist for CS to send to customers.

Known blockers / engineering constraints:
- Serving runtime currently does not have a stable server-side prompt cache API; adding one touches kernel selection codepaths. Need SRE review.
- Audit & billing: token accounting changes require finance sign-off and schema update to reflect savings vs usage.
- Private deployments: any automatic routing/fallback must be opt-in due to compliance and predictable latency guarantees.

Open questions to surface with product & eng:
- How should we measure customer-perceived UX improvements (replay, A/B)? Is session continuation adequate?
- For prefix canonicalization, what are privacy/security implications if prefixes contain PII? Need redaction guidance.
- What default TTLs are reasonable for different workloads (chat vs search vs classification)?

Suggested next steps (owner assignments):
- CS: run 6 more targeted interviews (Avery) — capture concrete flows and success thresholds by 2025-11-23.
- Eng (routing/serve): 1-week spike to validate feasibility of server-side canonicalization (Marcus Lee) — due 2025-11-30.
- Product: prioritize probes A & C for Q1 small-batch launch (Priya Raman to draft PRD sketch).
- Finance: initial review of token-billing changes and customer reporting requirements (Sofia Alvarez).

Appendix: short playbook/response templates for CS to use when triaging impulses:
- "We recommend enabling per-route embed TTL (24h) to reduce repeated embedding calls; we can enable as a temporary test and monitor token usage."
- "If you see occasional slow responses, enable 'degraded_mode' which will return a short placeholder and prompt a background retry; this has preserved session continuity in early tests."
- Quick checklist for customers: 1) identify repeated prefixes, 2) enable embed TTL, 3) add degraded templates, 4) monitor for behavior regressions.

Notes to self: keep this doc intentionally lightweight — purpose is to seed small experiments and to move away from triage ping-pong. If probes show >10% improvement on critical metrics, escalate to feature lane for Q2.

End of note.
